note: Triennial election of North Down Rural District Council, 1958 (Co. Down county and rural poll day Thursday 5 June 1958). Nominations closed on Tuesday 20 May: the one contest was in Kircubbin, where the retiring member Mr. James Boyd was challenged by Mr. Edward Floyd, a postman; in Kilmood the retiring member was deemed re-elected for want of a nomination; two new members came in for Carrowdore and Crawfordsburn; and thirteen other seats were filled by retiring members (Northern Whig, 21 May 1958, p. 9; Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958, p. 11, which lists the fifteen nominated). Quintin had no member from 1958 until 1964 ('has a representative on North Down Rural Council for the first time in six years', Belfast Telegraph, 20 May 1964, p. 4). No party labels were printed. Returned unopposed (retiring member). Division inferred from the 5 June 1952 return (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10); the 1958 reports name the member as returned but not his or her division.
